description: Modular feed-ranking interface + bounded, paginated feed queries in the Dart client. Replace the naive chronological, unbounded `select('*, profiles(*)')` in PostRepository with (a) a swappable FeedRankingStrategy abstraction so ranking logic can evolve (chronological now; personalized/recommended later) without rewriting the repository, and (b) keyset pagination (bounded page size, ordered by created_at desc, id) so the feed never issues an unbounded query and supports infinite scroll. Also align the client with the FEAT-002 server-owned counters: stop the client from writing repost_count directly (write to the reposts join table instead, mirroring the existing likes pattern) and stop writing reply_count. All new pure logic (ranking strategies, pagination cursor) MUST be unit-tested against the MockData path without booting Supabase, preserving the existing repository test contract.
steps: Create lib/data/feed_ranking.dart defining an abstract `FeedRankingStrategy` with a method like `List<Post> rank(List<Post> posts, {UserProfile? viewer})` (pure, synchronous, testable). Provide a `ChronologicalRanking` implementation (newest-first, the current behavior) and a `FollowingRanking`/scored placeholder implementation that documents where quality/engagement/freshness signals will plug in later. Keep the interface small and dependency-free so recommendation logic can evolve behind it. Document the design decision in a file-level doc comment (current approach -> why modular -> how to extend).

Introduce a keyset pagination cursor type (e.g. a small immutable `FeedCursor { DateTime createdAt; String id }`) either in feed_ranking.dart or lib/data/feed_page.dart, plus a `FeedPage { List<Post> posts; FeedCursor? nextCursor; bool hasMore }` result type. Choose a sensible bounded default page size constant (e.g. 20) — no hardcoded magic numbers scattered around; define it once.

Refactor lib/data/post_repository.dart to route forYou()/following() through the FeedRankingStrategy instead of an inline sort, preserving the EXACT current observable behavior for existing tests (forYou = all posts newest-first via ChronologicalRanking; following = followed-authors subset newest-first). The synchronous getters + single-notify + unmodifiable-view contracts that test/post_repository_test.dart asserts MUST remain intact.

Change the Supabase hydration query in PostRepository.load() to be bounded + keyset-paginated: add `.order('created_at', ascending: false).order('id', ascending: false).limit(pageSize)` and a `loadMore(FeedCursor cursor)` method that fetches the next bounded page using a `.lt`/or-composite keyset predicate (never an unbounded select, never offset-based pagination which degrades at scale). Keep it fully guarded (try/catch, mock fallback, notify only on real rows) exactly like the current load().

Align client with FEAT-002 server-owned counters: in toggleRepost's persistence, replace the direct `posts.repost_count` update (_persistRepostCount) with insert/delete on the new `reposts` join table keyed by (user_id, post_id), mirroring _persistLike. The optimistic in-memory repostCount stays a display estimate reconciled by the server trigger on next load(). Remove/adjust any client writes to reply_count. Update the code comments that described the repost_count drift limitation to reflect that it is now server-owned.

Add lib/data/feed_ranking_test.dart (or extend a test file) with unit tests for: ChronologicalRanking orders newest-first; FollowingRanking/scored strategy behaves as documented; FeedCursor round-trips / comparison; page-size bound is respected. Keep tests pure (no Supabase). Ensure test/post_repository_test.dart still passes unchanged (do NOT weaken it); if the public API shifts, adapt the repository so the existing assertions still hold, or update tests only where behavior intentionally and observably changed, documenting why.
Run analyze + test; fix any lints (the project is flutter_lints-clean and must stay so).
acceptance_criteria: lib/data/feed_ranking.dart exists with an abstract FeedRankingStrategy + at least ChronologicalRanking and one alternative strategy; PostRepository routes feeds through it rather than an inline sort
PostRepository.load() issues a BOUNDED query (explicit .limit with a single shared page-size constant) and there is a keyset-based loadMore(); no unbounded select and no offset pagination remain
Client no longer writes posts.repost_count directly; repost toggles write the reposts join table (insert/delete) mirroring likes; no client write to reply_count remains
New unit tests cover the ranking strategies and pagination cursor and pass; existing test/post_repository_test.dart still passes without weakening its assertions
`flutter analyze` reports 'No issues found!' and `flutter test` passes (baseline count + the new tests)
verification: export HOME=/tmp/fakehome PATH="/opt/flutter/bin:$PATH" PUB_CACHE=/opt/pub-cache && flutter analyze && flutter test
Confirm via grep/read that PostRepository.load() has an explicit .limit(...) and toggleRepost persistence targets the 'reposts' table, not a posts.repost_count update
findings: Implemented modular feed ranking + keyset pagination + reposts join-table alignment. Added lib/data/feed_ranking.dart (abstract FeedRankingStrategy.rank(posts, {viewer}) — pure/synchronous; ChronologicalRanking = newest-first current behavior; EngagementRanking = documented scored placeholder blending like/repost/reply/view signals with a newest-first tie-break, showing where a learned model plugs in) and lib/data/feed_page.dart (immutable FeedCursor{createdAt,id} with fromPost/compareTo/value ==+hashCode, FeedPage{posts,nextCursor,hasMore} with FeedPage.empty, and a single shared const kFeedPageSize=20). Refactored lib/data/post_repository.dart: forYou()/following() now route through the injectable _ranking strategy (default ChronologicalRanking) instead of an inline sort, preserving the exact newest-first + unmodifiable-view + single-notify contract; load() is now BOUNDED and keyset-ordered (.order created_at desc, .order id desc, .limit(kFeedPageSize)); added loadMore(FeedCursor) using an or-composite keyset predicate (created_at.lt OR (created_at.eq AND id.lt)) — seek-based, never offset, bounded to kFeedPageSize, guarded with mock fallback, de-dupes by id and notifies only on fresh rows. Replaced _persistRepostCount (direct posts.repost_count update) with _persistRepost that insert/deletes on the reposts join table keyed by (user_id,post_id) mirroring _persistLike; updated the comment to state repost_count is now server-owned by the sync_post_repost_count trigger from migration 0002. Confirmed no client writes to reply_count or repost_count remain (grep-verified; _postFromRow only READS them for display). Added test/feed_ranking_test.dart (9 tests: chronological newest-first + purity, engagement ordering + tie-break, FeedCursor round-trip/equality/compareTo, FeedPage empty + page-size bound). VERIFICATION: `flutter analyze` -> 8 issues found, exit 0 — exactly the pre-existing baseline INFO lints (withOpacity/prefer_const/dangling-doc/anonKey), NO new issues introduced. `flutter test` -> All tests passed (40 total: baseline 31 + 9 new); test/post_repository_test.dart passes unchanged (unmodified). Reverted the tooling-appended exclude block in analysis_options.yaml before commit (not staged). ENVIRONMENT RISK: no live/administerable Supabase project + no service-role key here, so the keyset .or() predicate, the reposts insert/delete RLS behavior, and the server-owned repost_count/reply_count triggers were verified by structural review only against migration 0002 — live keyset/RLS/trigger behavior is UNVERIFIED in this sandbox. No Android SDK/emulator, so no apk/device verification was possible (per context.json). REVIEW PASS v1 (addressing 2026-09-08-112626-review.md): (Issue 1 FIXED) _postFromRow was dropping the viewer's own liked/reposted state — load()/loadMore() now fetch the viewer's own likes/reposts post-id sets via a guarded _viewerEngagement() (scoped by user_id, empty on unauth/failure so the MockData fallback path is preserved) and merge them into mapped posts; extracted a @visibleForTesting static PostRepository.mapPostRow(row, {likedIds, repostedIds}) so the row->model hydration is unit-testable without booting Supabase, and added 6 mapping tests to test/post_repository_test.dart (counts/author mapping, default-false flags, liked/reposted hydration independently, counts-untouched, absent-id). (Issue 2 FIXED) keyset loadMore/FeedPage/FeedCursor were dead code — wired scroll-triggered infinite scroll into home_feed_screen.dart: _FeedList is now stateful with a ScrollController that, within ~600px of the bottom, derives a FeedCursor from the last post and calls PostRepository.loadMore, guarded against overlapping/exhausted fetches (_loadingMore/_hasMore) and against Supabase-unavailable (loadMore returns FeedPage.empty in tests/offline). (Issue 3 JUSTIFIED) keyset .or() predicate against PostgREST remains verified by structural review only — no reachable/administerable Supabase project or service-role key in this sandbox (documented environment risk, unchanged). VERIFICATION after review pass: flutter analyze => 8 issues (baseline INFO lints only, none in the changed files), flutter test => 64/64 pass (58 prior + 6 new mapping tests). analysis_options.yaml tooling exclude-block reverted, not committed.
